title.narrative: Strengthening water science, innovation, education and management in Ecuador

description.narrative: Ecuador as part of the Andean countries share a significant diversity within numerous ecosystems in four regions: the Andes, the Amazon, the Coast and the Galapagos islands. The country has a great number of indigenous communities mostly in the highlands and the amazon, which represents a good source of unique ancestral knowledge, that needs to be duly incorporated in public policies for climate change mitigation, disaster risk reduction, water management and, in general, sustainable development. In order to raise awareness and strengthen the visibility of young and indigenous voices, the Quito Office will work with those minority groups in order to involve them in the projects and initiatives. In this context, water-related challenges remain a highly relevant political, institutional and cultural issue. The Quito Office has been supporting Andean countries in several water related topics, in particular water education, through activities in Galapagos, the role of youth and civil society, through virtual and physical participation in Forums, Congress, and Seminars. Now, in this 2024-2025 biennium, the office will build on current progress and needs in Ecuador. In particular through supporting the strengthening and active participation of the IHP national committee (CONAPHI). Also, the Office will encourage collective reflection and the exchange of experiences among Andean countries, related to water education challenges and priorities, through the CONAPHI as well as through eco-hydrology sites.
